• Strengthens secularism and democratic values in Québec's public and private schools.
  • Adds rules on uncovered faces, religious symbols, and the quality of education services.

  • Students must have their face uncovered in schools, vocational training centres and adult education centres.
  • Children schooled at home and their parents must also have their face uncovered when receiving services.
  • Anyone providing services to students or in contact with them must have their face uncovered.
  • Students must respect equality between women and men and must not engage in bullying or violence.

  • Vocational training centres and adult education centres must also have codes of conduct.
  • The ban on wearing religious symbols is extended to staff of school service centres and certain contract workers.

  • Staff requests for religious accommodation to be absent from work are more strictly regulated and sometimes prohibited.

  • People providing services to students, members of governing boards and administrators must act without regard to religion.

  • School service centres must adopt a code of ethics for members of governing boards.
  • School and centre premises can no longer be used for religious practices.
  • No one may, for religious reasons, try to influence a decision made under this Act.
  • Teachers must submit a teaching plan to the principal, who must evaluate it every year.
  • A new committee on the quality of education services helps school administrations monitor teaching quality.
  • The Minister of Education can set the exam schedule and require a school service centre to comply with a law or regulation.
  • Certain decisions by the Minister, such as suspending a teaching permit, apply even if the teacher challenges them in court.

• This bill brings in several measures from Québec's March 2025 budget, touching on taxes, vehicles, support payments, and municipalities.
  • It also adjusts several related laws without major changes for the public.
Part 1 Act respecting the Québec Pension Plan
  • Work will only count as being done in Québec if it is also done in Canada.
  • The calculation of benefits will exclude months in which a person receives a reduced CNESST indemnity.
Part 2 Highway Safety Code
  • The vehicle value threshold triggering an additional fee rises from $40,000 to $62,500.
  • Electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles lose their exemption from this fee between $40,000 and $75,000 in value.
  • A new additional fee will apply to the registration of electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles.
Part 3 Act respecting the Institut de la statistique du Québec
  • Clarifies the rules when the Institute collects information for a public body.
  • More researchers linked to a public body will be able to access information for research purposes.
Part 4 Code of Civil Procedure
  • Changes the way the portion of a parent's income that can be seized for support payments is calculated.
  • Support payments made to an adult child can no longer be seized from the income of the parent receiving them.

  • A parent receiving financial assistance from the state will no longer have to provide a guarantee for the collection of support payments.
  • In the event of a declared emergency, the Minister of Finance will be able to set special rules on fees and advances related to support payments.
Part 6 Tax Administration Act
  • The calculation used to define a "large corporation" will take into account the capital of related corporations.
  • Tax information may be shared with the Minister of Finance, without the person's consent, to analyze economic or budgetary policies.

  • Life insurers will be able to obtain information about a deceased person in order to inform beneficiaries of amounts owed to them.

  • Municipalities will no longer be able to levy a business tax, except for certain fees from business development corporations.
  • Municipalities will no longer be able to establish a rental value roll for businesses.

  • The fee to consult the land register, which lists properties, will be revised.

26771:
• This bill merges several public bodies, abolishes others, and simplifies administrative rules in many sectors.
  • It also strengthens the accountability of senior officials and eases certain reporting requirements.
Part 1 Act respecting the National Institute of Excellence in Health and Social Services and Act respecting the Institut national de santé publique du Québec
  • Merged into a single body, the Institut québécois de santé et de services sociaux.
Part 2 Act respecting health and social services governance
  • Urgences-santé's board of directors will become the same as that of Santé Québec, the body that manages the health network.
Part 3 Act respecting Héma-Québec and the Biovigilance Committee
  • Héma-Québec takes over coordination of organ donations, a role previously held by Transplant Québec.
Part 4 Act respecting the Administrative Tribunal of Québec
  • This tribunal will now provide administrative services to the Financial Markets Administrative Tribunal.
Part 5 Act respecting the general and vocational colleges (CEGEPs)
  • The Commission d'évaluation de l'enseignement collégial, which evaluated CEGEPs, is abolished.
Part 6 Act establishing the Office Québec-Monde pour la jeunesse
  • This body is dissolved and its activities move to the Ministère des Relations internationales et de la Francophonie.
Part 7 Act respecting the Office franco-québécois pour la jeunesse
  • Its internal organization is revised.
Part 8 Act respecting the Centre de la francophonie des Amériques
  • The Centre continues to exist, but as a non-profit organization rather than a public body.
Part 9 Charter of the French Language
  • The Minister of the French Language gains new responsibilities regarding the Canadian Francophonie.
Part 10 Act respecting parental insurance
  • The Conseil de gestion de l'assurance parentale is abolished; Retraite Québec now manages this plan and its fund.
Part 11 Act respecting the Ministère des Finances
  • The Minister of Finance will have to present a comprehensive financial plan for fighting climate change during the budget speech.
Part 12 Act respecting the Ministère du Développement durable, de l'Environnement et des Parcs
  • The government will be able to decide, by a rule without a new vote, how to split surpluses from the Electrification and Climate Change Fund between the Generations Fund and the Land Transportation Network Fund.
Part 13 Act respecting the Ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale
  • This ministry's Information Technology Fund is abolished, with its assets and debts transferred to the government's general fund.
Part 14 Act respecting the Ministère de l'Enseignement supérieur
  • The Fund for University Excellence and Performance is abolished in the same way.
Part 15 Act to combat poverty and social exclusion
  • The Fund to Support Autonomous Community Action and the Québec Social Initiatives Fund are merged into a single fund.
Part 16 Public Service Act
  • The Public Service Commission is abolished; its functions move to the Administrative Labour Tribunal.
Part 17 Act respecting the marketing of agricultural, food and fish products
  • The Régie des marchés agricoles will have fewer vice-presidents and will be able to decide certain cases with fewer board members.
Part 18 Act respecting the Société de l'assurance automobile du Québec
  • The government will now appoint the SAAQ's vice-presidents and set their salary and working conditions.
Part 19 Act respecting Hydro-Québec and Act respecting the governance of state-owned enterprises
  • The management of the CEO of Hydro-Québec, the Commission de la construction du Québec and other state-owned enterprises will be discussed at least once every 4 years before a parliamentary committee.
Part 20 Public Administration Act
  • Senior officials (state administrators) will have to act with prudence, diligence, efficiency and fairness toward the state.
  • A new employee appointed as a state administrator will have to complete a 2-year probationary period.
  • During this probationary period, the government will be able to dismiss the state administrator with only 15 days' written notice, if the person was not already a permanent public servant.
Part 21 Act respecting contracting by public bodies
  • Businesses will no longer need to renew their authorization to contract with the state once obtained.
Part 22 Act respecting the Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales
  • Its contracts and those carried out for certain groups of bodies will follow the same rules as those of government enterprises.
Part 23 Act respecting the Société d'habitation du Québec
  • The government will be able to merge housing bureaus or create new ones for any chosen territory.
  • Joint management of financial contributions from beneficiary organizations is ending.
Part 24 Several laws in the financial sector (Act respecting the regulation of the financial sector, Securities Act, etc.)
  • Reduced frequency of certain reports and removal of the requirement to produce certain documents.
Part 25 Act respecting the regulation of the financial sector
  • The Autorité des marchés financiers, which oversees financial institutions, will have to make certain data and analyses available online.

• Changes the way MNAs are elected: a mixed system with 80 ridings and 17 regions.
  • Increases the number of seats in the National Assembly, from 125 to 129.
  • Creates two types of seats: 80 riding seats and 49 regional seats.
  • Each voter votes twice: one vote for a riding candidate, one vote for a regional list or an independent regional candidate.

  • Regional seats are shared based on the votes obtained in each region, with rules to balance results between parties.
  • A party must get at least 4% of the votes in Québec to be entitled to regional seats.
  • Parties must present as many women as men on their regional lists, alternating, starting with a woman at least every other time.
  • During general elections, each party must present between 40% and 60% women among its riding candidates.
  • Adjusts party financing rules and election spending limits, while keeping roughly the same total budget.
  • Sets out how to replace an MNA if a regional seat becomes vacant.

• This bill aims to better protect used vehicle buyers from hidden debts or rights tied to the vehicle.
  • It requires these rights to be checked before a sale and provides for compensation in case of an error.
Part 1 Highway Safety Code
  • A person selling a passenger vehicle must guarantee to the buyer that it is free of any rights.

Part 3 Consumer Protection Act
  • Merchants selling a used car will have to include the result of their check of the register of personal and movable real rights on the mandatory label.

• This bill creates two new acts on public safety and amends several other existing acts.
  • It deals with public disclosure about certain sex offenders and regulates demonstrations and symbols of criminal entities.
Part 1 Act respecting the public disclosure of information concerning certain sex offenders at high risk of reoffending
  • Creates a committee that decides whether information about sex offenders should be made public.
Part 2 Public Disclosure Act
  • The Sûreté du Québec and Correctional Services must send the committee information set out in a rule made by the government.
  • The government decides, through a rule, without a new vote, who is a "sex offender" covered by this act.
  • Information made public about a sex offender cannot remain public for more than 3 years.
  • A sex offender concerned can challenge the decision before the Administrative Tribunal of Québec.
  • The Sûreté du Québec must release the information according to what the committee has decided.
  • Sets out how disclosed information must be updated and how a decision can be reviewed.
Part 3 Act to promote peace, order and public safety in Québec
  • Bans demonstrating within 50 metres of the home of a member of the National Assembly, an elected municipal official or an elected warden.
Part 4 Peace, Order and Public Safety Act
  • Bans having or throwing certain dangerous objects or substances during a demonstration.
  • Allows a police officer to search a person and their surroundings if they believe the person has such an object, and to seize it.
  • Bans, except in certain cases, publicly displaying an object linked to an entity on a list of entities with criminal purposes established by the minister.
  • Sets the rules for adding an entity to this list.
Part 5 Police Act
  • Allows the minister to decide which gendarmerie services can be shared between police forces.
  • Allows other police services to be shared between police forces.
  • Allows the creation of Indigenous police boards to manage a shared police force.
  • Sets the status, makeup and operation of these Indigenous police boards.
  • Allows a board to sign an agreement with the government to have an Indigenous police force in its territory.
Part 6 Act respecting access to documents held by public bodies and the protection of personal information
  • Sets out the cases where a police force can share personal information with an organization or a victim.
Part 7 Private Security Act
  • Changes the rules on the length of the term of members of the board of directors of the Bureau de la sécurité privée.
Part 8 Act respecting the Québec correctional system
  • Allows a victim to read their own written statements at certain hearings of the Commission québécoise des libérations conditionnelles.

  • Technical changes to keep them consistent with the new acts.

26993:
• This bill simplifies the rules that professional orders must follow and gives more powers to the Office des professions du Québec, which oversees these orders.
  • It also allows several health professionals to do more things than before without waiting for a doctor's approval.
Part 1 Professional Code
  • Professional orders will be able to adopt certain regulations without the approval of the Office or the government, if they follow the Office's guidelines.
  • The Office, rather than the government, will now approve codes of ethics and regulations on activities carried out by non-members.
  • The Office will be able to decide which diplomas give access to a permit or a specialist title.
  • The Office will have to create a common rule for all orders on the conciliation and arbitration of professionals' accounts.
  • The Office will be able to adopt rules that apply to one or more professional orders, after consulting those orders.
  • The Office alone will decide on ethics rules for members of the orders' boards of directors, and will be able to investigate and impose penalties.
  • The public roll of each order (list of members) will have to contain more information than before.
  • The minimum number of signatures required to request a special general meeting of an order is changed.
  • People who obtained a psychotherapist permit under new pan-Canadian rules will be able to practise psychotherapy in Québec.
Part 2 Act respecting nurses
  • Nurses will be able to initiate examinations and tests in more situations, not only in public health.
  • They will also be able to prescribe examinations, medications, other substances, products and dressings, according to rules yet to come.
  • The rule reserving the right to vote to section delegates is removed.
Part 3 Midwives Act
  • Midwives will be able to prescribe and provide contraception, and screen for sexually and blood-transmitted infections, in more cases.
  • They will be able to treat these infections in a person without symptoms whose screening test is positive.
Part 4 Optometry Act
  • Optometrists will have fewer restrictions on the medications they can prescribe and provide, and on the care they can offer.
Part 5 Dietitians-nutritionists
  • Their scope of practice is updated and they will no longer need a medical prescription for certain reserved activities.
Part 6 Psychotherapy
  • The Interdisciplinary Advisory Council on the Practice of Psychotherapy ceases its activities.
  • Marriage and family therapists will be able to practise psychotherapy without a specific permit, like psychologists and doctors.
  • The Office will be able to authorize people in training to carry out certain activities reserved for psychotherapists.
Part 7 Act respecting agronomists
  • An act no longer needs to be performed for payment to count as the practice of the agronomist profession.
Part 8 Pharmacy Act
  • The government will be able to allow a pharmacist to prescribe or replace a medication with another made by a company in which they have a financial interest, under specific conditions.
Part 9 Act respecting prescription drug insurance
  • A new rule will allow a drug manufacturer to pay certain benefits to an intermediary, such as a pharmacy banner or chain.
Part 10 Regulation respecting drug manufacturers and wholesalers
  • The same benefits may also be paid by a manufacturer to a wholesaler.
  • Several acts affecting other orders (land surveyors, notaries, the Barreau, denturology, medical imaging technologists) receive governance or consistency adjustments related to the changes above.
  • Other technical consistency amendments are made to various acts and regulations, including the Charter of the French Language and the Act respecting legal aid.
